stacks.why: Text names the empty-months moment and flips the cause (waiting, not referrals), and spoken 'sign three clients, then you wait' is specific and sets up the text, but it is less clear about the feast-and-famine swing and has no twist of its own.

The misread flip ('not gaining weight, swollen') is a real contrast and text and spoken are one claim, but 'she' and 'swollen' never say who it is for or why, so sound-off buyer lock is weak; the same line twice adds nothing, and there is no cause or fix promised.

Spoken is strong: 'You doubled your cold emails' is a specific, countable failed fix and the first line is the reason; the text never says 'cold emails', so sound-off buyer lock is thin and 'replies' alone is ambiguous.

Spoken states the feast-or-famine problem plainly with a countable 'three clients', but 'literally' is filler and it does not echo the 'waiting' cause in the text, so the seam to the claim is looser than S01.

Text qualifies the buyer best ('some months full, some empty') in 9 words and flips the referral belief, though 'aren't the problem' is a softer twist than 'waiting'; spoken is the same specific line as S01 and fits this text well.

Text uses 'your kidneys' (meta check fail) and a generic fear line with an unsupported medical claim (foam as kidney failure); spoken has a twist in the speaker (the kidneys), but sentence 1 is long (about 19 words), the problem arrives after 'I'm your struggling kidneys', and it is fear-baiting rather than calm.
